questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which finding best distinguishes sepsis from an uncomplicated infection?
choices: A positive culture alone
New life-threatening organ dysfunction associated with the response to infection
Fever above 38°C in every case
An elevated white blood cell count without clinical change
questions.explanation: Sepsis requires dangerous organ dysfunction related to infection. Fever, leukocytosis, or a positive culture can occur without sepsis, while sepsis can occur without any one of those findings.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement about sepsis screening is most accurate under the 2026 guideline?
choices: qSOFA alone should rule sepsis in or out
A normal temperature excludes sepsis
NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS, or SIRS is preferred over qSOFA as the single screening tool, but no score replaces clinical assessment
A lactate result alone establishes the diagnosis
questions.explanation: The 2026 SSC guideline favors NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS, or SIRS over qSOFA as a single hospital screen. Sepsis remains a clinical diagnosis and no score or biomarker independently confirms or excludes it.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient has probable sepsis, hypotension, confusion, and rapidly worsening perfusion. Blood cultures are difficult to obtain. What is the safest action?
choices: Delay all antimicrobials until cultures are complete
Collect cultures promptly if possible, but do not let difficult collection delay immediate authorized antimicrobial therapy
Wait three hours because every case allows an investigation period
Give an antipyretic and reassess tomorrow
questions.explanation: Cultures should be obtained as soon as possible and ideally before treatment, but probable sepsis with shock requires immediate antimicrobial therapy. Diagnostic logistics must not create a dangerous delay.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which assessment best helps determine whether another fluid bolus may improve perfusion?
choices: A single central venous pressure value
Dynamic change in stroke volume or pulse pressure during a passive leg raise, interpreted with the full examination
Lactate alone until it reaches zero
The presence of fever
questions.explanation: Dynamic measures such as response to passive leg raise or a small fluid challenge are preferred over static measures alone. They must be integrated with mentation, capillary refill, urine, lungs, pressure, and oxygenation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: After initial crystalloid, a patient remains hypotensive and develops crackles, rising oxygen needs, and no improvement in capillary refill. What is the priority interpretation?
choices: More fluid is always required until lactate normalizes
The patient may be fluid unresponsive and developing congestion; escalate for vasopressor and hemodynamic reassessment
Crackles prove the infection is cured
Stop monitoring because the patient already received 30 mL/kg
questions.explanation: Absent perfusion improvement plus congestion warns against automatic fluid escalation. The RN should report nonresponse and pulmonary findings and support individualized vasopressor and hemodynamic evaluation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement about vasopressor initiation in septic shock is correct?
choices: A needed vasopressor must always wait for central access
Norepinephrine is generally first-line, and protocol-guided peripheral initiation can avoid harmful delay while definitive access is arranged
Dopamine is first-line for every patient
The universal MAP target is 90 mm Hg
questions.explanation: Norepinephrine is the usual first-line vasopressor. Current guidance supports carefully monitored peripheral initiation when needed rather than delaying solely for a central line; MAP goals are individualized around an initial target.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient with septic shock has an abdominal abscess. Which plan addresses definitive treatment?
choices: Continue antimicrobials indefinitely without evaluating drainage
Arrange early source control, ideally within six hours when the source requires intervention
Wait for lactate normalization before consulting surgery
Use fever response to decide whether the abscess is real
questions.explanation: An abscess often requires drainage because antimicrobials cannot remove a walled-off source. Current guidance supports early source control, ideally within six hours when intervention is required.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement about lactate in sepsis is most accurate?
choices: It rises only because tissues have no oxygen
It is a useful risk and perfusion marker, but other processes affect it and fluid should not be continued solely until it normalizes
A normal value excludes sepsis
Every elevated result requires sodium bicarbonate
questions.explanation: Lactate can reflect multiple processes and must be trended with the clinical response. Persistent elevation prompts reassessment, but it does not justify unlimited fluid or routine bicarbonate by itself.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which cluster most strongly suggests worsening multiorgan dysfunction in sepsis?
choices: Improved mentation, brisk urine output, and reduced oxygen need
New confusion, oliguria, rising oxygen need, thrombocytopenia, and increasing bilirubin
One normal temperature reading
Stable appetite and mobility
questions.explanation: Progressive neurologic, renal, respiratory, hematologic, and hepatic abnormalities indicate expanding organ dysfunction. These changes require urgent reassessment even if one vital sign appears acceptable.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which finding best indicates that early septic-shock resuscitation is improving tissue perfusion?
choices: MAP, mentation, capillary refill, and urine output improve without worsening oxygenation or edema
Temperature remains elevated for one hour
More fluid has been infused regardless of response
The white blood cell count is unchanged
questions.explanation: Successful resuscitation is evaluated through a composite response in hemodynamics, brain, skin, kidneys, oxygenation, and congestion. Treatment volume or one laboratory result is not an outcome by itself.
